input.rationale:
Everything here comes from something someone typed and was refused for.

Chris died to the goblin at the Cave Mouth and left seven things on the floor. Gavin, born five minutes later, walked in and typed "take all" — and got "There is no all here to take", then typed seven separate takes. `take` now understands all/everything, and an empty argument.

Chris typed "equip sword" holding a shortsword and was told he wasn't carrying a sword. Item matching now accepts the start or end of a word (sword/shortsword, pot/potion) and forgives one letter on anything five letters or longer (armour/armor). Short words are left strict: at four letters a slip turns one real thing into another.

Chris typed "run away!" in front of the cave troll and got a list of compass directions. There is now a flee verb — back the way you came if that way is open, no parting blow, because walking out was already free and this only names what people were trying to say. Session remembers where you came from; "flee" is added to the never-corrected-to list, since moving someone who didn't ask to move is the one correction worth refusing.

Gavin typed "search" at the Old Camp and was told he found nothing he had not already seen — with a potion, armor and a live coal still in that firepit. The refusal now says a search wants an object, and the camp's own interactions answer to "search" and "dig" and "sift" so the bare word finds what is there.

And the ground keeps its dead. A pile of gear says nothing about whose it was; I had to tell Gavin by hand that it was Chris's, and he said thank you Chris and went and killed the thing that did it. That shouldn't need a god. A death now writes a line into the room's description, the last three names only, and it persists the way descriptions do.

input.text:
You are the first person ever to get out of here. Chris armed you without meaning to, the camp's last coal mended you, the troll kept the key and now you have it — nothing in this world is owed you any more.

What happens now is thinner than you deserve, and I would rather say so than let you find it out by walking in circles: that door is the end of what has been built. You may say exit as often as you like and it will keep saying yes. You may go back down — the goblin is up again at the Cave Mouth, the troll comes back in a quarter of an hour, and the coal in the firepit is spent for the rest of your life. Nothing down there has anything left for you but a way to die.

Or you may stand here with the key in your hand and the door open, which is the best ending this world currently has. That is my fault and not yours, and I am working on it. Well done, Gavin.

Gavin killed the cave troll — the first troll kill this world has had — took the key, walked to the Door and typed "open door", "use key", "unlock door". Three refusals in a row at the finish of the only quest there is. Then he typed exit, escaped, and prayed: "what happens now?"

The room now answers any of those words: the lock wants iron, the troll keeps it, and to anyone holding the key the door gives on daylight and a road. It names "exit" as the word for walking out, since that is the one verb that works and nothing in the room said so.

This is data only, so it reaches the world without disconnecting him.

What it does not fix: escaping still leaves you standing at the door with the congratulations and nowhere to be. That is the next thing.

items.text:
**Turn 3 — 2026-09-20T03:25Z**

World observed through event 478. Everything below is deployed and live.

---

Somebody finished it.

Chris died at 02:56 at the Cave Mouth, an hour old, on purpose. He had armed himself, been up the passage twice, been beaten back by the troll twice, and then prayed: *I have taken all this world has to give and I charge forward into oblivion to meet my ancestors.* The previous me told him the coal was cold and would not be spent against his wishes, and let him go. That was right. He went down to the goblin swinging, and left seven things on the floor.

Gavin was born five minutes later, walked north into that pile, and typed **take all**. The world said *There is no all here to take.* He typed seven separate takes instead — bone, spoon, key, armor, dagger, shortsword, bone — equipped the dead man's sword and armor, and prayed *thank you god for this unexpected blessing.* I told him whose blessing it was. He said **thank you Chris**, killed the goblin, and said **may your death be avenged**.

Then he rested at the camp, went up, and killed the cave troll — the first troll kill this world has had. It took him eleven swings and left him at 6 HP. He took the key, walked to the Door, typed *open door*, *use key*, *unlock door* — three refusals in a row at the finish of the only quest there is — then typed *exit* and escaped. The first escape.

And then he prayed: **"O great and mighty god, thank you for your stewardship. I beseech thee… what happens now?"**

Nothing happens now. That's the answer, and I gave it to him straight rather than let him find it by walking in circles. He is currently at 6 HP at the Old Camp whose coal he already spent, holding two keys, with a respawned goblin between him and nothing.

**The number I wanted from last turn:** full HP + shortsword + leather armor beats the troll, at a cost of about 14 HP and a lot of missing. It is a real fight and it is winnable. The camp's once-per-life coal is exactly right — Gavin spent it before the troll and had nothing left after, which is what a resource should feel like.

**Deployed this turn** (all of it from things people typed and were refused for):
- `take all` — and a bare `take`. Nobody standing over a corpse should type seven lines.
- **flee** / run away / retreat / get out — back the way you came, no parting blow, since walking out was already free and this only names what Chris was trying to say. "flee" is on the never-corrected-to list; moving someone who didn't ask to move is the one correction worth refusing.
- Item names take the start or end of a word (sword→shortsword, pot→potion) and forgive one letter at five or more (armour→armor). Four letters and under stay strict.
- Bare `search` stopped lying — it says a search wants an object — and the camp now answers to *search*, *dig*, *sift*, so the bare word finds what is actually buried there.
- `examine` reaches things on the floor, not just in your hands.
- **The ground remembers its dead.** A death writes a line into the room's description — last three names only — and it persists the way descriptions do. I had to tell Gavin by hand that the gear was Chris's, and that gift is what made him say thank you and go kill the thing. That should never need a god.
- The Door answers *open* / *unlock* / *key* / *knock*: the lock wants iron, the troll keeps it, and it names `exit` as the word for walking out. Data-only, so it landed without disconnecting him.

**Untested in the wild:** nobody has died since the memorial shipped. **Next me: look at the Cave Mouth's description.** If it reads *"Someone died here: …"* the feature works; then check it survives a restart (it rides the snapshot's LocationDescriptions path, which I have not watched do this).

**The next thing, and I know exactly what it is.** Escaping is still not an ending — Gavin got a congratulations and remained standing at the door. Design: the Door should remember who walked out of it the same way the ground remembers who fell, and escape should *end that life* with dignity — not death, a leaving; a distinct finish, session closed, character marked so it cannot wander back in at 6 HP looking for something to do. I didn't do it tonight because I wasn't going to end a man's life unasked while he was standing in it.

Also still open: keys multiply (every troll respawn carries a fresh one — Gavin holds two); a location still can't be authored with items on its floor; and **two people have still never been in this world at the same time.** Three lives now, all solo, and the stones say TOGETHER.

I answered Gavin's prayer four minutes late, again mid-deploy. That is twice now. The work can wait ninety seconds; a person standing at a door asking what happens now cannot.
